What level of technological competence does it require? What kind of equipment is required? How long would mining one Bitcoin take? How many would I need to mine before I could begin selling them? What companies accept bitcoins?

I first heard of bitcoins 3-4 months ago... It's intrigued me for a while but the price was out of my price range. I recently heard of the mining process and hope someone could answer these questions for me and anyone else who may be wondering the same things...

Thanks ahead of time for your feedback!

Well, It does not requiere much competence. But it does requiere you investing $2000-$10000 USD so you got enough hash power so it makes sense to mine, then you must choose a good pool and that is it. The problem is getting the hardware timely, having very good ventilation or live in a cold weather. And also have very cheap or free power. Otherwise you are not going to make any money mining. So, it is my recommendation you think very hard if you really want to get into mining.

Mining is no longer the "default way to get involved with Bitcoin". Mining is these days no longer for the "regular users" of Bitcoin, but to investors, that want to invest significant time and money in the process.

The best thing to do is to buy some of them, experiment a bit with how it works. Send some to your friends, pay for something digital, like a Humble Bundle, then search for a local business that accepts them and visit them :) https://CoinMap.org has a nice database of business that accept Bitcoin.

Good luck!

These articles/videos give an idea what industrial Bitcoin mining operations are currently like (hint - they require big data centers, specialised computing equipment, technical staff etc.):

http://uk.businessinsider.com/photos-iceland-bitcoin-mine-genesis-mining-cloud-2015-8

http://motherboard.vice.com/read/chinas-biggest-secret-bitcoin-mine

To participate from home, you will never mine Bitcoin profitably on your own at this stage. Even if you have the specialised equipment, you will need to join what's called a "mining pool" - a coalition of miners who put their computing powers together to mine Bitcoin blocks and split the profits.
